label: FP
reason: All three alerts are False Positives. Alert 1 (java/xss) and Alert 2 (java/path-injection) share the same data flow where user input 'param' is stored in a Map ('keyB-37053') but subsequently overwritten by a constant ('keyA-37053' -> "a_Value") before reaching the sink expressions (fileName). The resolved sink value is therefore a constant string, not user-controlled. Alert 3 (java/error-message-exposure) reports the error message 'e.getMessage()' which derives from the file access attempt on the same constant-based 'fileName'; thus the error message does not leak sensitive user data. Since all alerts resolve to safe, non-user-controlled values, the case is labeled FP.
